gpu: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 SXM (NVLink, 18 links x 26.5 GB/s)
status: measured on 2x H100 SXM (RunPod). Sharding verified argmax 8/8 vs single-GPU oracle on H100.

single_gpu_h100.note: on H100 the fused kernel is 2.2x off the weight floor (vs 1.21x on the 4090) -- fixed attention/small-matrix/launch overheads don't shrink when bandwidth is 3.3x larger, so they dominate a bigger share.

tensor_parallel_h100.code_path_note: TPDecoder has extra o_buf/d_buf fp32 copies + lm_head all-gather vs the plain model_graph path, so its TP=1 (2.815) is the fair same-code baseline for TP=2, not the 2.028 plain single-GPU number.

finding: Tensor parallelism did NOT speed up batch-1 decode here. Halving the per-GPU weights cut compute 2.815 -> 2.060 ms (saved 0.76 ms), but the per-layer all-reduce latency added 0.92 ms (2 all-reduce/layer x 28 layers, ~16 us each -- latency-bound on tiny 6KB payloads, not bandwidth-bound), cancelling the gain. TP=2 (2.975) ~= TP=1 (2.815). The honest lesson: TP wins batch-1 latency only when per-GPU weight-streaming time dominates the fixed all-reduce latency -- i.e. larger models or slower per-GPU bandwidth. On a fast H100 with a small model, comm latency wins, and TP is the wrong tool for single-stream latency.
caveats: NCCL collectives would not capture inside a CUDA graph on this stack (torch 2.4.1 + NCCL, even with NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 and pre-capture barriers -- it deadlocks). So TP=2 comm is measured EAGER: 56 all-reduce + 1 all-gather in a Python loop. Per-call launch overhead is NOT amortized, so 0.915 ms is an UPPER BOUND; a captured/fused comm path would be lower and could push TP=2 toward break-even.
Production TP fuses the all-reduces and overlaps compute/comm; at batch 1 there is little compute to overlap the comm with.
The qualitative conclusion (TP marginal for small-model batch-1 latency on a fast GPU) is robust regardless of the comm-measurement method.
